publication.title: iPhone OS Research Atlas
publication.scope: iPhone OS 1.1.4, build 4A102; original iPod reference and native PinePhone research
publication.provenance: Original editorial synthesis of private project notebooks and experiment reports, with reviewed capture images, selected source excerpts and their provenance. Firmware, storage images, complete run artifacts and the implementation repository are not included.

record.title: Later registration can replace a working interrupt callback
record.method: Registration trace and bounded integrated interrupt control
record.observation: A later legacy callback replaced the native nonsecure timer callback. The combined routing control delivered and returned from 51 timer interrupts, preserving earlier console and commpage evidence.
record.limits: The bounded run did not establish all interrupt sources or complete boot.

exhibits.title: Interrupt ownership changed after installation
rows: No completed-return count in this record
exhibits.interpretation: The legacy callback accepted SGI1, whereas the arriving nonsecure timer was ID 30. Registration overwrote the CPU callback field at offset 0xa4. The control counted both entry and return, rather than only interrupt arrivals.

exhibits.title: The next boundary remained visible
exhibits.interpretation: Progress through the timer path exposed another absent legacy device. It did not establish a full kernel boot.
